issues.description: Entire compiled script transferred in-band on every compile with no size bound
issues.detail: The RPC payload now includes the full script_content for every compile, regardless of size. For large pipelines this inflates response time and memory on both ends. The asymptotic cost is O(N) in script length per compile, paid even when the user never clicks Download. Prefer a lazy GET endpoint that streams the file on demand.

issues.description: File read lacks encoding declaration and error handling invariant
issues.detail: open(script_path) without encoding='utf-8' relies on the platform default — a portability bug waiting to happen. There is also no invariant stated for what happens if the file is missing or unreadable after compile_pipeline; the exception will propagate and discard the already-computed package_path. State the invariant: script_path exists and is UTF-8 after successful compile.

issues.description: Blob MIME type misrepresents Python source
issues.detail: type: 'text/plain' is incorrect for a .py file; the conventional choice is 'text/x-python' or 'application/octet-stream' to force download. text/plain may cause some browsers to render rather than download, defeating the feature when the anchor download attribute is ignored (e.g., cross-origin object URLs in certain embeds).

issues.description: Download control is an icon click with no keyboard affordance or button semantics
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick is not a button: no role, no tabindex, no Enter/Space handler. titleAccess provides a label but the element is not focusable. Wrap in an IconButton (or a real <button>) so the readable invariant — 'this is an actionable control' — holds for keyboard and assistive-tech readers.

issues.description: Object URL revoked synchronously after click; literate comment missing
issues.detail: URL.revokeObjectURL is called immediately after a.click(). In most browsers this is fine because the download is initiated synchronously, but the invariant ('download has started before revoke') is not stated and is browser-dependent. A two-line comment explaining the click-then-revoke contract would make this readable without running it.

issues.description: Filename derivation uses compiledPath but content is the pre-compile script
issues.detail: compiledPath points to the compiled .yaml/.tar.gz package, while script_content is the intermediate .kale.py script. Splitting compiledPath to derive a .py filename conflates two artifacts; the resulting filename can mislead the user. Either send the script's own basename from the backend or rename the prop to make the invariant explicit (compiledScriptName vs packagePath).

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The feature works but the analysis is missing on two axes. First, the backend pays an unbounded O(N) cost shipping the entire script over RPC on every compile whether or not the user downloads — a lazy endpoint would respect the 'don't optimize without measuring, but don't ship obvious waste either' principle. Second, the frontend control lacks button semantics, uses an imprecise MIME type, and revokes the object URL on an unstated invariant. None are catastrophic; all are exactly the kind of small rigor a literate reading would catch before merge.
